title: HEATING SYSTEM UPGRADES
description:
The purpose of this requirement is to upgrade the heating system at Marks Farm Community Centre and Silver End Village Hall, as well as the supply and installation of a new Photovoltaic Array on the roof of Silver End Village Hall. 

Silver End Village Hall is a large community centre in Silver End. Its main use is to provide a community facility for local residents. It has a changing room to the rear managed by Braintree District Council and current tenant's, include a Social Club, Silver End Parish Council offices, ECC Family Hub and small to medium sized events business, who hire out their space to a nursery, a library and for events. 

Marks Farm Community Centre is a medium sized community centre in Braintree. Its main use is to provide community facilities for local residents. It has a changing room to the rear managed by Braintree District Council and its current tenant is a small to medium sized events business, who hire out their space to a nursery and also for events.

The existing heating systems in both buildings have reached the end of their serviceable life and are now life expired, resulting in increasing maintenance needs and risk of failure. The refurbishment will replace outdated components, improve accessibility, renew mechanical and electrical systems, and ensure compliance with current building, health and safety and landlord obligations. The works will also support ongoing lettability of the building's and contribute to maintaining statutory standards such as minimum energy efficiency requirements.

title: Continued provision of Web Casting via  Braintree District Council EPHF001 Webcasting framework
description:
Southend-on-Sea City Council is looking for continued provision of Web Casting services using the current equipment installed by Public-I Group Limited. The contract will include the provision of web casting in the Council Chamber of council meetings, links to the Civica Modern.gov system for the delivery of meeting papers for councillors and the public. The equipment for the Council Chamber is leased from Public-I and this contract includes the replacement of equipment as nears end of life.

Southend-on-Sea City Council has investigated the possibility of going out to the market with the potential of a new provider reviewing the web casting needs and potentially installing new equipment, however the Local Government Reorganisation introduces a possibility that a new Mayoral Combined Council (MCC) may host its Full Council meetings outside of Southend.

It was decided that it not be economically advantageous for Southend-on-Sea City Council to undertake a procurement exercise to replace all the web casting equipment in the Council Chamber and Committee Rooms, if the new system would not be used. If the new MCC is established, all contracts will be reviewed. If the new MCC decides that this contract should be procured early, then a compliant procurement process will be undertaken.

title: EPP0114 - Clare Road Play Area
description:
Braintree District Council welcomes interested parties to participate in this tender for the 
refurbishment of the Clare Road Play Area. This project, funded under Section 106 (S106), 
aims to enhance the recreational facilities within our community whilst adhering to the 
highest safety standards.
Located at pods.forkful.blog (What Three Words location), the Clare Road Play Area requires 
comprehensive revitalisation to ensure it remains a vibrant hub for children and families alike. 
As part of this endeavour, the Council has outlined a detailed specification that encompasses 
the replacement and enhancement of existing play equipment across both open field areas 
and the toddler (fenced) play area.
In line with Framework Agreement PROC20-0107, prospective bidders are invited to submit 
proposals for various aspects of the refurbishment project. This includes the removal and 
replacement of outdated equipment with new installations designed to promote inclusive and 
engaging play experiences.
Crucially, all proposed works must meet stringent safety requirements, with particular 
attention paid to overlaying wet pour safety surfaces and creating no-edge surfaces to 
mitigate potential hazards. Additionally, post-installation inspections are integral to this 
tender, ensuring the ongoing safety and longevity of the refurbished play areas.
The scope of work spans from the removal and replacement of swing bays and inclusive 
roundabouts to the revitalisation of trim trails and toddler play equipment. Furthermore, 
measures such as weed control and surface overlay are essential components to be addressed 
within the tender proposals.
Braintree District Council invites capable and experienced contractors to submit 
comprehensive bids that align with the outlined specifications. Through collaborative efforts, 
we aim to rejuvenate the Clare Road Play Area, providing a safe, inclusive, and enjoyable 
environment for generations to come.
Prospective bidders are encouraged to carefully review the provided specifications and submit 
their proposals by the designated deadline. Should you require any further clarification or 
information, please do not hesitate to contact the Council's procurement team.
This tender has a maximum budget of £82,666.10.

title: CO0587 - Essex ActivAte Programme (HAF) 2025
description:
The Department for Education has provided Essex County Council with funding in order to deliver the holiday activity and food programme (HAF) across Essex during the Easter, Summer and Winter school holidays. Active Essex will be managing the programme on behalf of Essex County Council. Active Essex and Essex County Council will also be managing the HAF programme on behalf of Thurrock Council. Across Essex and Thurrock the programme is called Essex ActvAte. \r
\r
Essex ActivAte will engage and support young people and families who are eligible for benefits based free school meals and families most in need. The programme will provide free and inclusive holiday clubs across the county that will include a range of fun physical and enrichment activities, a free nutritious meal, nutritional education and mentoring and support for the young person and whole family. The programme aims to improve health generally, including, crucially, mental health and aim to provide the families with the knowledge and support to live healthier, happier lives.  \r
\r
We are looking for delivery partners or consortiums who can lead and deliver Essex ActivAte clubs across Essex and Thurrock during the main school holidays.  \r
\r
The Essex ActivAte programme has now been running for 3 years, working with over 300 delivery partners to offer over 150,000 free spaces and hot meals per year. Over the next year of 2025, it is our aim to extend the programme so that every young person who is eligible for benefits based free school meals or is in need of this holiday support has the opportunity to engage in a local club. \r
\r
Key outcomes of each Essex ActivAte club are:\r
â€¢	To provide free and inclusive holiday activity clubs for eligible young people\r
â€¢	To provide a safe environment for young people to attend in the school holidays\r
â€¢	To provide a fun, high quality holiday club experience for the young people\r
â€¢	To support the social skills of the young people attending\r
â€¢	To provide mentors and role model through the Essex ActivAte club staff\r
â€¢	To ensure that young people have at least 1 nutritious meal each day\r
â€¢	To provide education for the young people and whole family around eating more healthy, nutritious meals, on a budget\r
â€¢	Providing signposting and support for the whole family so that they have the understanding and knowledge to improve their physical and mental health and wellbeing, support network and opportunities. \r
\r
The maximum bid value per project is £300,000.
